correctness.rationale: All structural steps are reconstructed: minimum edge covers correspond exactly to onto words; replacing either duplicated position with a blank gives a bijection to edges of the permutation-star Cayley graph; adjacency is equivalent in both directions; regular bipartite root and line-graph properties yield counts, triangles, chromatic and independence numbers; the star-word metric follows from a cycle split/merge count and explicit factorization; a simultaneous extremal pair of root edges realizes the line graph upper diameter bound. Direct independently constructed finite adjacency sets and breadth-first distances agree for stated ranges. Computation does not substitute for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The minimum edge-cover exchange problem is a natural constrained optimum reconfiguration model. The first imbalance beyond perfect matchings has an exactly solvable connectivity transition, full line-graph structural equivalence, sharp optimal-step diameter and triangle/degree invariants. These give transport of a rich routing metric to combinatorial optimum solutions and do not follow from the minimum edge-cover number alone.
